read.sections.0.text.back: An invention is a new tool, machine or way of doing something. About 5,500 years ago, people in Mesopotamia used the wheel to shape clay pots. Later, people fitted wheels to carts to carry heavy loads of grain and goods, and this made farming and trade easier. Printing is another example. About 1,000 years ago in China, a man named Bi Sheng made small blocks out of clay, each one with one writing mark. Printers could move the blocks to print new pages. Later, printers in Korea used metal blocks. In the 1400s, Johannes Gutenberg built a printing machine in Germany. Books became cheaper, so more people were able to read and share ideas.
read.sections.0.text.source: An invention is a new tool, machine or way of doing something. About 5,500 years ago, people in Mesopotamia used wheels to shape clay pots. Later, people put wheels on carts to carry heavy loads of grain and goods, which made farming and trade easier. Printing is another example. About 1,000 years ago in China, a man named Bi Sheng made small clay blocks, each with one written sign. Printers could move the blocks around to print new pages. Later, printers in Korea used metal blocks. In the 1400s, Johannes Gutenberg built a printing press in Germany. Books became cheaper, so more people could read and share ideas.

read.sections.0.simpler.back: An invention is a new tool or way of doing something. Long ago, people in the place now called Iraq used the wheel to make pots. Later, people fitted wheels to carts to carry heavy things. Printing is also an invention. In China, Bi Sheng made small blocks out of clay. Each block had one mark. Later, people in Korea made metal blocks. After that, Gutenberg made a printing machine in Germany. Books became cheaper, so more people were able to read.
read.sections.0.simpler.source: An invention is a new tool or way to do something. Long ago, people in what is now Iraq used wheels to make pots. Later, people put wheels on carts to carry heavy loads. Printing is another invention. In China, Bi Sheng made small clay blocks, each with one sign. Later, people in Korea made metal blocks. Then Gutenberg made a printing press in Germany. Books cost less, so more people could read.

read.sections.1.text.back: Some newer inventions spread very quickly. Mobile phones let people make calls, send messages and look for information. In Kenya, a service that started in 2007 lets people send small amounts of money by phone, even without a bank. Solar lamps are another example. In the daytime, sunlight charges the battery inside the lamp. At night, the lamp gives light without any electric line. In the past, many families used lamps that burn kerosene, which give off smoke and have to be bought again and again. With solar lamps, people can cook, read or study after dark. But inventions only help people who have access to them.
read.sections.1.text.source: Some newer inventions spread very quickly. Mobile phones let people call, send messages and find information. In Kenya, a service that started in 2007 lets people send small amounts of money by phone, even without a bank. Solar lamps are another example. During the day, sunlight charges a battery inside the lamp. At night, the lamp gives light without any power lines. Many families once used lamps that burned kerosene, which made smoke and had to be bought again and again. With a solar lamp, people can cook, read or study after dark. But an invention only helps people who have access to it.

read.sections.2.text.note: Back-translation check: Fixed: 'manakala' (whereas) set up a false contrast. It is now a separate sentence with 'pula'.
read.sections.2.text.back: Look at the bicycle trial in Riverstone. Cycling to the market takes 12 minutes, not 30 minutes, so Amara saves 18 minutes. That is a real benefit. But a bicycle costs 80 tokens, and Hana cannot afford to pay for it, whereas repairs need spare parts and skills. The steps on the direct route are a barrier, because riders must carry their bicycles up the steps. Some people cannot ride a bicycle, or do not want to. Inventions can also cause problems that nobody planned. Cars make travel faster, but cars also make the air dirty. So, when you study an invention, ask who can use it, who makes the decisions and what could help more people.

write.example.back: This trial shows that cycling saves Amara 18 minutes on the direct route to the market. One benefit is that she has more time for other work. However, one barrier is cost. A bicycle costs 80 tokens, so Hana cannot own one. The steps on the direct route are also a barrier. Before giving out more bicycles, I would test the longer route without steps. I would also ask whether people can share bicycles. This would help more people because more of them would be able to use bicycles safely.
write.example.source: The trial shows that cycling saves Amara 18 minutes on the direct route to the market. One benefit is that she has more time for other work. However, one barrier is the cost. A bicycle costs 80 tokens, so Hana cannot get one. The steps on the direct route are also a barrier. Before giving out more bicycles, I would test the longer route with no steps. I would also ask if people could share bicycles. This would help more people because more of them could use one safely.

Check that this phrase is clear, and check the tone of 'orang yang diperhambakan' (enslaved people). watch.summary.back: This video tells the story of the cotton seed separating machine (cotton gin), which is a machine invented in the United States in 1793. The cotton plant produces soft white fibre, which is used to make cloth. Before there was this machine, workers had to remove the seeds from the cotton by hand, and this work was very slow. This machine did that work much faster. One worker could now do the work of about 10 people. Growing cotton began to make more money, and the cotton business grew quickly. But this machine also brought very bad effects that nobody planned. Cotton plantations became bigger, and plantation owners forced more enslaved people to work on the plantations. Slavery continued for longer. This video shows that one invention can bring wealth and also great harm.
watch.summary.source: This video tells the story of the cotton gin, a machine invented in the United States in 1793. Cotton plants grow soft white fibre, which is used to make cloth. Before the machine, workers had to pull the seeds out of the cotton by hand, and this was very slow. The cotton gin did the job much faster. One worker could now do the work of about 10. Growing cotton began to earn much more money, and the cotton business grew fast. But the machine also had a terrible effect that no one planned. Cotton farms grew, and farm owners forced many more enslaved people to work on them. Slavery lasted longer. The video shows that one invention can bring both wealth and great harm.
